name: Coinbase
description: Coinbase runs a crypto trading and custody platform for retail consumers, institutions and developers. Its largest source of revenue is fees on crypto trades: for consumers a flat fee or a percentage of each transaction plus a spread, and for institutions a fee schedule that falls with volume. The fastest-growing source is 'subscription and services', chiefly stablecoin revenue: under an agreement with Circle (issuer of USDC), Coinbase is paid a share of the interest earned on the reserves backing USDC, and the more USDC is in circulation generally and on Coinbase, the more it earns. It also takes a share of staking (blockchain) rewards, interest and finance-fee income, custody fees and subscriptions. About 84 percent of FY2025 revenue was in the U.S. Revenue depends heavily on crypto prices and trading volume; H1 2026 total revenue fell 25.4 percent from H1 2025 and the company reported a net loss.

gics.note: Conventional label recorded from general knowledge of the standard scheme; not re-checked against an MSCI/S&P source in this pass. SEC SIC code is 6199 (Finance Services), from the EDGAR submissions record. The box does not describe the revenue mix: in FY2025 about 59 percent of net revenue was trading fees but about 41 percent was subscription and services, of which stablecoin revenue alone was $1.35B (USDC reserve income shared by Circle) and blockchain (staking) rewards $0.68B.

hq.note: One Madison Avenue, Suite 2400, New York, NY 10010 is the address of principal executive offices on the FY2025 10-K cover; the registrant is incorporated in Texas (10-K cover). Whether the company still calls itself remote-first was not checked.

businessLines.name: Transaction revenue
businessLines.how: Retail and institutional customers pay a flat fee or a percentage of each trade (plus a spread on consumer buys and sells), every time they trade; revenue rises and falls with trading volume and crypto prices. Bitcoin and Ethereum pairs drove about 45% of Trading Volume in 2025 (46% in 2024).
businessLines.description: Fees charged when customers buy, sell, trade or convert crypto assets on Coinbase, split into Consumer, Institutional and Other transaction revenue.

businessLines.name: Subscription and services revenue
businessLines.how: Mostly balance-driven, not volume-driven: Circle pays Coinbase a share of the reserve income on USDC (more revenue the larger the share of USDC in circulation and held on Coinbase), Coinbase keeps a commission on staking rewards earned by customers' staked assets, and it earns interest and fees on customer and corporate balances and loans. Monthly subscriptions and custody fees make up part of 'other'.
businessLines.description: Recurring and balance-based revenue: stablecoin revenue, blockchain rewards (staking), interest and finance-fee income, and other services (custody, Coinbase One subscriptions, and other items).

revenue.note: FY2024 $2,307.1M (+23%); FY2023 $1,406.9M. H1 2026 $1,138.7M vs $1,306.9M in H1 2025 (-12.9%), but not comparable: from Q1 2026 revenue earned on corporate payment stablecoin balances moved out of net revenue into Other revenue (10-Q Note 2)

businessLines.how: Yield on Coinbase's own cash and stablecoin holdings; rises and falls with balances and interest rates rather than customer activity.
